name: password-input
purpose: Password field built on a native password <input>: label, help text, localized validation, a show/hide toggle (aria-pressed), autocomplete for password managers (current-password / new-password), an optional Caps Lock warning, and a clipboard policy. The value never appears in events, messages, or announcements. It is an input, not an authentication provider.
whenToUse: Any secret the user types and may want to check visually (show/hide).
whenNotToUse: One-time codes and PINs: use OTP Input.
As a replacement for server-side password policy or authentication.
responsive: Full width of its container; the toggle keeps a control-height square at the inline end.
rtl: Logical properties: the toggle sits at the inline end in both directions.
theme: Same control surface, border, focus, and error tokens as Text Input; the Caps Lock warning uses color-warning-fg with an icon. Forced-colors mode draws a Highlight outline on focus.
security: The value is never included in events (details carry validity only), validation messages, or announcements. spellcheck is off (spelling services may send text off-device) and autocapitalize is none. autocomplete defaults to current-password so password managers work. The clipboard policy is a deterrent, not a security boundary; the default allows paste. Edge's built-in reveal control is hidden to avoid a duplicate toggle. Credential handling, hashing, and policy enforcement belong to the application and server. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: The value lives only in the native input. No persistence, logging, network access, or telemetry.

performance.testedScale: 1,000 inputs on one page in the performance test.

limitations: Caps Lock state is known only after a key or mouse event in the field (browsers expose it through getModifierState).
Revealing shows the password on screen: shoulder surfing is the user's decision.
Manual screen-reader verification (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) is pending.
unsupported: Rendering HTML in the label, help text, or messages.
Storing or remembering passwords (password managers do this).
antiPatterns: Putting the password in a validation message or analytics event.
Changing the toggle's accessible name together with aria-pressed.

adapters.angular: @absoluteui/angular/password-input: AuiPasswordInput directive ([auiPasswordInput]) with ControlValueAccessor (string) and Validator.
adapters.react: @absoluteui/react/password-input: AuiPasswordInput component; controlled (value/defaultValue + onValueChange) or uncontrolled.
